reason: Conversation 2 gave a sensible first step straight away: it checked for anything touching the panel, dried the panel and power-cycled at the cooker switch. It was honest that E011 could not be confirmed, and it ranked a pressed or moisture-affected key as the likeliest cause. When the customer reported success, it explained the residue cause, gave prevention tips and said when an engineer would be needed. Conversation 1 guessed a main PCB fault, gave an irrelevant instruction about setting the clock after a power cut, asked a vague question, and then escalated to an engineer without ever suggesting drying the panel or a power reset. That was unnecessary and pointed towards an unjustified repair.
